note: Game functions by name (SDK 16, hellforge_functions.h): each one's place in its module (rva), its first bytes as reviewed (code, an IDA-style pattern the loader checks before every use, through other hooks), its C signature and what each argument is. hook: true only where the signature is whole (every argument the function takes, unnamed ones as pass-through slots, and its return value), so a detour passes everything on; the others are for calling. The loader resolves them only on this build: a new game build revalidates every entry.

params.name: mix_id

EntityOfNetwork.meaning: The entity a network id names on this machine now, written to out (and out returned). hf->entity_of_network is the checked way to call it

StratagemAvailable.meaning: Whether the player has a stratagem available to take, as the picker's heading counts it

params.meaning: not reviewed: pass it on (DamageEvent +0x60, kept in the record at +0x40)

params.name: s18
params.meaning: not reviewed: pass it on (DamageEvent +0x20, the hit-ring key)

ApplyDamage.meaning: Applies one damage to an entity's health: acceptance mask, element and Vitality multipliers, zone health, downing and death (KillDispatch). ConsumeDamageEvent calls it with the DamageEvent's fields, on the machine that drains the queue
ApplyDamage.source: HD2Runtime 0.40.1 research event-combat (damage_apply, 15 stack args); ConsumeDamageEvent's call at 0x12A82EB

IsDead.meaning: 1 when the entity's health record says dead (life state +0x19C >= 2); 0 when alive, downed or without a health record

HealthRecord.meaning: The entity's health record (0x1B8 bytes in the HealthManager's records at +0x1058). An entity with no record gives a bad pointer, not NULL: check first. No code calls it

params.name: fraction
params.meaning: the health to set, as a fraction of the maximum

RestoreHealth.meaning: Sets an entity's health to fraction x its maximum and revives a downed one (life state 0); does nothing to the dead. The stim's status handler calls it

HealthSettings.meaning: The entity's HealthComponentData: its private copy if it has one, else the shared type record (0x5650 bytes each)

params.name: index
params.meaning: the health record index (not the entity)

params.name: state
params.meaning: the new life state (0 alive, 1 downed, 2 dead)

params.name: kind
params.meaning: the damage kind that caused it

params.name: element
params.meaning: the damage element that caused it

SetLifeState.meaning: Raises a health record's life state (+0x19C; a lower state is ignored) and runs what follows the change. ApplyDamage calls it, and the update calls it when the replicated state differs

HealthManagerUpdate.meaning: The HealthManager's frame update: regeneration, time since damage, damage-over-time deaths and the replicated life state

DrainCombatQueues.meaning: The frame's drain of the combat queues: up to 16 damage events per call through ConsumeDamageEvent, then the status and other queues
DrainCombatQueues.source: HD2Runtime 0.40.1 research event-combat (queue_drain); HD2Runtime 0.40.1 research event-actions

params.name: event
params.meaning: a whole DamageEvent (0x70 bytes) to copy

EnqueueDamageEvent.meaning: Copies a DamageEvent into this machine's damage queue (CombatQueues +0x1120, 4096 at most; a full queue drops it). No code calls it

params.name: hit
params.meaning: the hit event (+0 kind, +4 element, +0x20 target, +0x84 dealer and +0x104 owner network ids, +0x110 creditor)

ProduceDamage.meaning: Turns a hit into a queued DamageEvent (damage = trunc(values +0) times the target's attribute) and queues the hit's status effects when the armour factor is not 0. Every damage source's hit goes through it
ProduceDamage.source: HD2Runtime 0.40.1 research event-combat (producer); HD2Runtime 0.40.1 research direct-hit-damage

params.name: source
params.meaning: the source struct (+0xC, +0x1C hit node, +0x20, +0x24 DamageInfo id)

InitHitInfo.meaning: Fills a hit event from its source: target, hit zone and armour, and the DamageInfo row's element and damage
InitHitInfo.source: HD2Runtime 0.40.1 research event-combat (hit_init); HD2Runtime 0.40.1 research direct-hit-damage

EntityToNetwork.meaning: The network id of an entity (EntityOfNetwork's inverse); 0x7FFF when it has none

HealthZoneOfNode.meaning: The health zone a hit node belongs to (zones at settings +0x208, 0x228 bytes each, 38 at most); the default zone (settings +0x40) when none lists it

BuildDamageValues.meaning: Builds a hit's DamageValues with the builder of its kind (+0 damage, -1 to kill; +4 armour factor) and returns values

IsBoosterActive.meaning: 1 when the mission has the booster (ApplyDamage asks it for Vitality, id 1)

params.name: buildup
params.meaning: the strength, against the target's susceptibility

ApplyStatus.meaning: Applies a status to an entity owned here: susceptibility and buildup decide, then the type's handler runs. Weather Insulated (56) refuses 53..55

HasStatus.meaning: 1 when the entity has the status

RemoveStatus.meaning: Ends a status on an entity: the type's handler runs with apply = 0

params.name: source
params.meaning: the source entity, or the invalid entity to use resource

params.name: resource
params.meaning: the source resource, read when source is the invalid entity

AddStat.meaning: Adds amount to one of a player's mission stats, overall and under its source. Kills, deaths, stims, shots and damage all count through it
AddStat.source: HD2Runtime 0.40.1 research event-combat (add_stat); HD2Runtime 0.40.1 research event-state (addStatCallSites)

StatsPlayerIndex.meaning: The ScoreManager index of the player with this peer id (through PlayerManager +0x2C8); 0xFFFFFFFF when none

params.name: map
params.meaning: the map: +0 entries (20 bytes each, u32 key first), +8 capacity, +0xC empty key, +0x10 hash multiplier

StatMapLookup.meaning: The 20-byte entry of a u32-keyed map that holds key, or the empty slot that ends its probe; NULL when the map is full. The stat tables use it (an entry's +4 is the stat's value)

params.name: score
params.meaning: the score to fill: +0 dealt_damage, +4 dealt_kills, +8 dealt_team_kills, +0xC melee kills, +0x10 team damage, +0x28 stims used, +0x30 reinforcements called, +0x34 received damage

BuildScore.meaning: Fills a player's end-of-mission score from the stat keys

params.name: creditor
params.meaning: the peer the kill is credited to

params.name: dealer
params.meaning: the entity that dealt the killing damage

params.name: element
params.meaning: the damage element: passed, not read

KillCreditListener.meaning: KillDispatch's listener that counts a kill in the creditor's mission stats (dealt_kills, team kills, melee kills) when the victim's KillScore is above 0
KillCreditListener.source: HD2Runtime 0.40.1 research event-combat (kill_credit); KillDispatch's call at 0xB96392

PassiveValue.meaning: A value after one passive's modifiers of a key: (the last Set, else base) plus every Add, times every Multiply; base when the passive has none

params.name: data
params.meaning: passed to the new state's enter handler; may be NULL

ChangeState.meaning: Changes the game state: runs the old state's exit handler, writes Game +0xAC21C and runs the new state's enter handler (Mission zeroes the StateGame block). HF_ON_STATE polls the value it writes

SetPlayerAvatar.meaning: Sets a player's avatar (+0x108 + 0x70 per owned player, network id at +0x3A8 + 0x20 per player) and its state to Spawned (3)

params.name: state
params.meaning: the lifecycle state (2 WaitingForRespawnTimer, 3 Spawned; 0 and 1 unnamed)

SetPlayerState.meaning: Sets a player's lifecycle state (PlayerManager +0x2E0 + 0x38 per player)

params.name: descriptor
params.meaning: the entity's descriptor (+8 the entity); NULL gives NULL

TurretSettings.meaning: The entity's TurretComponentData (0x4C bytes: +8 vertical, +0xC horizontal turn speed): its own copy in the turret manager (game.dll+0x3326D70, copies +0xA8) if it has one, else the shared type record

params.name: descriptor
params.meaning: the entity's descriptor (+8 the entity); NULL gives NULL

SensorEyeSettings.meaning: The entity's SensorEyeComponentData (0x2C bytes: the vision ranges the sensor copies at spawn): its own copy if it has one, else the shared type record

params.name: descriptor
params.meaning: the weapon entity's descriptor (+8 the entity); NULL gives NULL

ProjectileWeaponRecord.meaning: The weapon's ProjectileWeaponComponentData (+0 the projectile type): its own copy in ProjectileWeapons if it has one, else the shared type record
ProjectileWeaponRecord.source: HD2Runtime 0.40.1 research component-swap-liberator-beam; HD2Runtime 0.40.1 research beam-conversion-add-layout

params.name: descriptor
params.meaning: the weapon entity's descriptor (+8 the entity); NULL gives NULL

WeaponDataRecord.meaning: The weapon's WeaponData record (0x4D0 bytes; fire modes, the input bindings): its own copy in WeaponDatas if it has one, else the shared type record

params.name: descriptor
params.meaning: the weapon entity's descriptor (+8 the entity); NULL gives NULL

BeamWeaponRecord.meaning: The weapon's BeamWeaponComponentData (+0 the beam type): its own copy in BeamWeapons if it has one, else the shared type record

WeaponProjectileType.meaning: The projectile type the weapon fires now, by its components: the magazine's round type or pattern, WeaponRounds' primary or alternate magazine, linked ammunition, else ProjectileWeapon +0

params.name: type
params.meaning: the projectile type to fire; 0: the weapon's own (WeaponProjectileType)

ProjectileFire.meaning: Fires one shot of a weapon's projectiles; type 0 resolved to 0 fires nothing. The ProjectileWeapon update, the heat step and GenericFire all shoot through it
ProjectileFire.source: HD2Runtime 0.40.1 research fired-type-callers (fire 0x6128B0); HD2Runtime 0.40.1 research beam-conversion-add-layout (projectileFire)

params.name: type
params.meaning: the projectile type; 0: the weapon's own

GenericFire.meaning: The generic fire: hands the shot to ProjectileFire (its arguments 5 to 11 pass through) when the weapon has a ProjectileWeapon or ArcWeapon instance, else returns. Charged releases and the heat levels fire through it
GenericFire.source: HD2Runtime 0.40.1 research fired-type-callers; HD2Runtime 0.40.1 research beam-conversion-coverage (genericFire)

WeaponHeatStep.meaning: Adds one shot's heat to a weapon with a WeaponHeat instance and fires the projectile of the heat level reached (its own type per stage)
WeaponHeatStep.source: HD2Runtime 0.40.1 research beam-conversion-add-layout (heatStep); HD2Runtime 0.40.1 research fired-type-callers

SpendRound.meaning: Spends one round of a weapon (magazine, rounds or linked ammunition), shared by every output family; the beam spends one per pulse

ProjectileWeaponUpdate.meaning: One ProjectileWeapon instance's frame: its fire timer and trigger, then the shot (through the heat step when the weapon has WeaponHeat)

BeamWeaponUpdate.meaning: One BeamWeapon instance's frame: the charge gate and the beam shot from the trigger byte
BeamWeaponUpdate.source: HD2Runtime 0.40.1 research beam-conversion-add-layout (beamUpdate); HD2Runtime 0.40.1 research beam-damage-per-weapon

BeamShot.meaning: One beam pulse: spends a round and runs the heat step of the weapon's own WeaponHeat; no authority test on the way

ReloadMagazine.meaning: The reload refill: spends one spare magazine (one unit from the parent's deposit when shared) and fills the magazine, queuing the network field writes

TurretUpdate.meaning: The turret system's frame: turns every turret toward its targeting direction, yaw then pitch, with the instance's turn speeds and the settings' limits (TurretSettings, resolved every frame)

TurretSpeedFactor.meaning: A new turret's turn speed factor from the ship-module modifiers (1.0 by default); turret creation stores it in the instance at +4

params.name: sensors
params.meaning: the sensor eye manager (entity map at +0x30)

params.name: scale
params.meaning: the factor for the SensorEyeSettings ranges

SensorEyeRanges.meaning: Sets a sensor's vision ranges in its instance (+0xC, +0x10, +0x14) to its SensorEyeSettings ranges times scale and keeps scale at +0x20

PerceptionUpdate.meaning: The perception frame: every perceiver's sensors mark what they sense (the proximity sensors without a line-of-sight ray)

WindUpUpdate.meaning: The weapon wind-up frame: spin progress rises by dt / settings +0 while the trigger is held; on release settings +4 <= 0 resets it, else it falls by dt / settings +0

params.name: value
params.meaning: the value to modify in place

ApplyAttribute.meaning: Applies the entity's armour or helmet modifier of a key (EntityAttribute with flags 3) to *value: Set stores, Add and Time add, Multiply multiplies; no modifier leaves it. No code calls it

UpdateCustomization.meaning: Moves one player's pending customization to the applied record; when the new kit's package is ready it copies the kit ids and sets the applied armour and helmet passives (+0x3C, +0x38) from the kit

UpdateCustomizations.meaning: The customization frame: UpdateCustomization for every record, then the 2 passive ids of every player slot, loading and unloading their packages when they change

SetArmorKit.meaning: Sets a player's pending armour kit (pending record +0xC, network field 0xB7D3A2EC); UpdateCustomization applies it and its passive

SetHelmetKit.meaning: Sets a player's pending helmet kit (pending record +4); UpdateCustomization applies it and its passive

SetCapeKit.meaning: Sets a player's pending cape kit (pending record +8)

PlayerSlot.meaning: A player's slot (0 to 3), kept at PlayerManager +0x3B4 + 0x20 per player; the customization update reads each slot's passives with it
PlayerSlot.source: HD2Runtime 0.40.1 research player-attributes (updateAll: 0x606820 = player slot of an entity)

params.name: context
params.meaning: the behaviour's context (+0 the entity's descriptor)

params.name: node
params.meaning: the hash of the unit node it goes off at

BehaviourExplosion.meaning: Requests an explosion at a node of the behaving entity's unit: into the ExplosionQueue (RequestExplosionAt) and to the peers. Enemy behaviours and abilities call it
BehaviourExplosion.source: HD2Runtime 0.40.1 research event-actions (behavior explosion wrapper); HD2Runtime 0.40.1 research explosion-identities

RequestExplosionAt.meaning: Queues an explosion request at a position through RequestExplosion; BehaviourExplosion and the ability explosion wrapper use it
RequestExplosionAt.source: HD2Runtime 0.40.1 research event-actions; HD2Runtime 0.40.1 research explosion-identities (0x13C6D30)

params.name: explosions
params.meaning: the explosion system (the ExplosionQueue's object, Game + 0x1C9DAF8)

ExplosionKick.meaning: Starts this frame's explosions: up to 8 queued requests (kicked count at +0x24), early in the world update

ExplosionGather.meaning: Finishes the kicked explosions later in the same world update (ProcessExplosion for each, in order) and moves the rest of the queue to the front

params.name: offset
params.meaning: the request's offset in the explosion system: 0x28 + 0x98 per entry

ProcessExplosion.meaning: Processes one kicked explosion request: its hits, damage and effects
ProcessExplosion.source: HD2Runtime 0.40.1 research event-explosions (process one explosion); event-actions (the game drains the queue)

ProjectileKick.meaning: The projectile step of the world update, after the explosion kick: its impacts request explosions after the kick

params.name: context
params.meaning: the behaviour's context (+0 the entity's descriptor)

BehaviourStartAbility.meaning: Starts an ability on the behaving entity: StartAbility with the AbilityManager, mode 1 and speed 1.0, returning its result
BehaviourStartAbility.source: HD2Runtime 0.40.1 research event-actions (ability play); HD2Runtime 0.40.1 research pelican-cas

CorpseSource.meaning: For a corpse (Corpses global), the descriptor of the entity it came from; NULL when the entity is no corpse. Entity removal consults it

StatusReceivable.meaning: 1 when the entity can receive the status (StatusReceivers' susceptibility rule, the same as ApplyStatus's); the status queue checks it first
StatusReceivable.source: HD2Runtime 0.40.1 research event-actions (the target can receive the type); acid-storm-attachment

FlushNetworkFields.meaning: The sync point: flushes every batched network field write (clamped and sent), before and after the frame's update phases

params.name: item
params.meaning: the item entity held in the slot

Wield.meaning: Puts an item in a wielder's slot (slot record +0 holds the entity) and wields it. The weapon switch calls it

params.name: selection
params.meaning: the slot to select (record +0x1C; 1..5 pick record +0, +4, +8, +0x10)

SwitchWeapon.meaning: Selects an inventory slot and wields its item (Wield)

params.name: network
params.meaning: the object's network id (0x7FFF: nothing is queued)

params.name: value
params.meaning: the live value (read when the batch is flushed)

QueueFieldWrite.meaning: Queues one replicated field write {network id, field hash, value pointer} in the batch (0x800 entries) that FlushNetworkFields clamps and sends; every replicated gameplay field change goes through it
QueueFieldWrite.source: HD2Runtime 0.40.1 research ammo-network-fields; component-swap-liberator-beam (network field write)

BeamTypeOf.meaning: The weapon's beam type: BeamWeaponRecord +0, re-read at every shot; 0xFFFFFFFF for the invalid entity

OutOfAmmo.meaning: The out-of-ammo handler: returns at once when the weapon has a WeaponReload instance; otherwise it uses the weapon's WeaponData (its AutoDropAbility, the expendables' drop)

params.name: type
params.meaning: the projectile type of the charge level; 0: the weapon's own

ChargeFire.meaning: Fires a charged release through GenericFire with its own type (the charge level's projectile). The charge release 0x73D8C0 calls it
ChargeFire.source: HD2Runtime 0.40.1 research fired-type-callers (callers of the charge fire 0x741A00); HD2Runtime 0.40.1 research beam-conversion-coverage

params.name: entity
params.meaning: the entity resource's hash (an armory entry's +8, a weapon's entity)

EncyclopediaRecord.meaning: The entity's EncyclopediaEntryComponentData record (component 76; +0 its name text id, +0x24 its designation text id), by open addressing over 1330 slots; NULL for 0 or an entity without one

PickerCatalogueItem.meaning: The player's catalogue item (24 bytes, at account + 0xB9CE4) for a stratagem type, or NULL when the catalogue has none: what the picker's heading counts as selectable before StratagemAvailable

params.name: resource
params.meaning: the entity resource's hash (a moving object's +0)

NavigationRecord.meaning: The resource's Navigation component record (+4 its navigation profile hash, +8 a radius), by open addressing over a static table; NULL for 0 or a resource without one

BehaviourStageCount.meaning: How many stages a behaviour has; 0 for an unknown id, and such an entity never enters stage 1. HellForge points its id check at a stub that answers for its own behaviours with their base's count

BehaviourEventSlot.meaning: The network slot a behaviour sends an event in; 0x1F when the behaviour does not replicate it. Paired with BehaviourSlotEvent; HellForge's stub answers for its own ids with their base's slot

params.name: slot
params.meaning: the network slot an event arrived in

BehaviourSlotEvent.meaning: The event hash a behaviour's network slot stands for, as a replicated event is turned back into one; 0 for none. The inverse of BehaviourEventSlot

params.name: candidates
params.meaning: the candidates, 12 bytes each: x, y, and +8 the squared distance it writes

params.name: centre
params.meaning: the reference point (x, y): SpreadLocations passes its reference location's cluster centre, +0xE0

FillDistancesTo.meaning: Writes each candidate's squared 2D distance from a point into its third float, before SpreadLocations sorts them by it (comparator 0xF7A5A0). SpreadLocations read location -1 here on level-11 city maps until HellForge gave it location 0
FillDistancesTo.source: HellForge's location spread fix (difficulty.c DIF_SPREAD_REFERENCE); research d11-map-centre

params.name: image
params.meaning: the image element: +0x114 its base UV rect (4 floats), +0x134 the sprite sub-rect (x, y, w, h)

UpdateImageUv.meaning: Recomputes an image element's UV rect (+0x124..+0x130) from its base UV and its sprite sub-rect; a sub-rect of 0, 0, 1, 1 copies the base. HellForge's difficulty icon stub resets the sub-rect and ends here
UpdateImageUv.source: HellForge's difficulty bar icons (difficulty.c); HD2Runtime's stratagem slot icons (uv_for)

HiveMindDefinition.meaning: The resource's shared HiveMindComponent definition (0x43C bytes; +0x74 the mission countdown in seconds), by open addressing over 38 slots; NULL for none. The mission spawn and the war table's mission card copy it and apply deltas; the shared one is never written

params.name: clear
params.meaning: nonzero: also zero the DamageInfo list's 650 slots (0x1450 bytes at game + 0x37C60C0)

UnloadDamageList.meaning: Releases the damage list's resource and, when asked, clears the DamageInfo id list (called through a table, not directly). A reload never clears past slot 649, so HellForge's moved list keeps its added rows

params.name: unused
params.meaning: not read (callers leave the value they store in s5)

params.name: rdx
params.meaning: not reviewed: pass it on (callers pass a u16 of their descriptor, +0x10; it goes on to 0x12DF110)

params.name: r8
params.meaning: not reviewed: pass it on (-1 or a looked-up id; it goes on to 0x12DF110)

params.name: difficulty
params.meaning: the difficulty level (callers pass a byte, their descriptor's +0x20)

params.name: s5
params.meaning: not reviewed: must equal the operation row's u32 before its highest difficulty (6 adds an account check)

params.name: s6
params.meaning: not reviewed: must equal the operation row's u32 4 bytes below its lowest difficulty

params.name: rows
params.meaning: receives the index (0..24) of each matching operation row

CollectOperationsForDifficulty.meaning: Collects the operation settings rows (25 of 0x490, lowest and highest difficulty at +0xC / +0x10) that allow a difficulty and match the caller's kind, and returns how many: the war table's mission board only offers a level they allow, so HellForge lets every row allowing 10 allow 11

params.name: pass
params.meaning: the pass context: +0 the generation arena, +8 = lg+0x2D20 (the level's radii)

params.name: r8
params.meaning: not reviewed: pass it on (FinalizeVoronoi passes a {u32 count, u32, pointer} list of its own; the weld reads count and pointer)

params.name: r9
params.meaning: not reviewed: pass it on (a second {u32, u32} list, cleared and filled by the weld)

FinalizeVoronoiStructured.meaning: FinalizeVoronoi on structured maps (map type 2: mega cities, factories): welds vertices through a 24 x 24 bucket grid whose blocks come from a pool of 512 (+0xBA60, 0xA08 each, count +0x14CA60); 0 on failure. HellForge gives the pool 576 blocks

params.name: rcx
params.meaning: not reviewed: pass it on (a {u32 count, u32, pointer} list from the pass's state, 32-byte entries)

params.name: rdx
params.meaning: not reviewed: pass it on (a second such list)

params.name: r8
params.meaning: not reviewed: pass it on (the pass's state +0)

params.name: pass
params.meaning: the pass context: +0 the generation arena, +8 = lg+0x2D20 (the level's radii)

params.name: s5
params.meaning: not reviewed: pass it on (the level + 0x1990)

params.name: count
params.meaning: an output count it zeroes first

ReVoronoi.meaning: Level generator op 0xA3 (revoronoi) on structured maps: refills the land around the city with a Poisson disc at the nature cell size (+0x18C), kept apart from the city's sites; returns the new diagram or NULL. HellForge grows the cell size on larger maps

PlaceRoadProps.meaning: Places one road prop of a city street (its caller runs it rand % type+0x230 + 1 times per edge), testing the position against its rule's reach (+0x54) past the playable radius. HellForge measures that reach from the border on larger maps

params.name: x1
params.meaning: the area's highest x (the map's size)

StampIndexInit.meaning: Sets up the level generator's stamp index over an area: placed stamps, locations and roads by cell, for overlap tests (10757 slots after a bitset; slots + 1 at +0x1C). HellForge gives it 16383 slots
StampIndexInit.source: HellForge's larger maps (difficulty.c stamp index sites)

params.name: slot
params.meaning: receives the slot's cell mask, or 0 when the index is full

StampIndexInsert.meaning: Takes a free slot of the level generator's stamp index for a rect and links it into every cell the rect covers; returns the slot's record (callers write the stamp's id at +0) or NULL when full (17 callers; a full index used to be written through that NULL)
StampIndexInsert.source: HellForge's larger maps (difficulty.c stamp index sites)

params.name: rcx
params.meaning: not reviewed: pass it on (the pass dispatcher passes its rsi + 8)

params.name: unused
params.meaning: not read (the pass dispatcher passes its rsi)

params.name: pass
params.meaning: the pass context: +8 = lg+0x2D20 (the level's radii), +0x18 the level (lg)

CreateMinimapTexture.meaning: Level generator pass: captures the level's minimap texture with the level's radii

params.name: card
params.meaning: the war table's mission card widget

params.name: mission
params.meaning: the mission descriptor: +9 its level, +0x1A its mission row (u16), +0x1D its modifier count, +0x20 the modifiers

UpdateMissionCardDuration.meaning: The war table mission card's duration: the mode's HiveMind definition with only the mission row's delta (+0x360) applied in a copy, its seconds divided by 60 into the card's minutes (0x1A131CC). HellForge shows the added level's own countdown there

params.name: get_api
params.meaning: the engine's API getter, (u32 id) -> API table; it asks for ids 0x28, 0x1F, 6 and more

SetupPhysicsConfig.meaning: game.dll's plugin setup_game, once per process (from its plugin table, no direct caller): takes the engine's APIs, then fills the engine's physics config with its pool sizes, from which the exe builds every world's pools. HellForge raises those sizes before it runs

params.name: unused
params.meaning: not read (its caller passes hf_global_WeaponLinkerManager's cell)

SiloRemoteLink.meaning: A silo remote's link, which its laser update runs every frame: while the remote's linker record says a silo link (+4 0x06212002) and the missile is not launched yet, it launches it (engine, explosive set off), names the explosive's owner, sets its guidance target to the laser's point and has the rack let it go. HellForge's silo countdown repeats these steps in this order

params.name: designators
params.meaning: the laser designators (the world system passes its + 0x75C2B8)

LaserDesignatorUpdate.meaning: Updates every laser designator for a frame (a silo remote's laser) and calls each remote's link (SiloRemoteLink), which launches the missile on the first frame the laser marks a point

params.name: unused
params.meaning: not read (its thunk loads a manager into it)

LinkRemoteOnPickup.meaning: Links a silo's targeting remote to its missile when it is picked up: the rack's items in the SeekingMissile manager, and the missile's +8 names the remote's network handle. Reached through a component callback thunk (0x528870)

params.name: unused
params.meaning: not read (its thunk passes the event in both)

params.name: event
params.meaning: the component event: +8 the entity (the missile), +0xC compared with the remote's attachable record

MissilePreDestroy.meaning: A seeking missile's pre-destroy callback: on the machine with authority over its remote, takes the remote out of its holder's hands, looking it up among the attachables and reading the record unchecked. HellForge guards that read (engine 0.1.21, InstallLooseGuard) for a remote attached to nothing

params.name: unused
params.meaning: not read (its thunk passes the event in both)

params.name: event
params.meaning: the component event: +8 the entity; +0x10 what it returns

CompactLinkerCopies.meaning: A WeaponLinker's destroy callback: drops the entity's linker copy and moves the last copy into the freed slot, so a record pointer kept across frames can name another remote's. Returns the event's +0x10

params.name: linkers
params.meaning: the linker manager its caller walks

params.name: r8
params.meaning: not reviewed: pass it on (its caller's index)

params.name: r9
params.meaning: not reviewed: pass it on (the linker record; +8 read)

SiloRemoteCleanup.meaning: Removes a silo remote once it is dropped and its rack is gone (ability 2089); runs only for a silo link, so a remote whose linker record HellForge marked as no link stays until the launch

PelicanTurretAim.meaning: Behaviour 645's (the Pelican's chin turret) stage 2, aim: at least 1.5 s, until within 2 degrees of its target, re-scoring its perceiver's entries. HellForge's turret aims without the wait

params.name: index
params.meaning: the weapon's component index (not its entity)

params.name: type
params.meaning: the projectile type chosen (a programmable round may replace it, 0x615B23)

params.name: transform
params.meaning: the shot's transform: +0x10 its direction, +0x30 its position

params.name: owner
params.meaning: the owner or wielder entity (its creditor comes from Creditor)

params.name: s6
params.meaning: not reviewed: pass it on (copied into the pool's options)

params.name: s7
params.meaning: not reviewed: pass it on (a shot random or token)

params.name: s12

params.name: components
params.meaning: the entity manager's component callbacks (EntityManager + 0x40): one array of 324 function pointers per callback kind, indexed by component type

params.name: record
params.meaning: the new entity's world record (+0 the entity, u64; +0x10 its network id, u32; +0x14 its flags)

params.name: info
params.meaning: the SpawnInfo SpawnEntity was given: +0 authority byte (1: this machine is in charge of it)

params.name: ids
params.meaning: the object at EntityManager + 0x8: the spawned entity's id goes into its table at +0xB020

SpawnEntityAddComponents.meaning: SpawnEntity's first component pass: for each of the new entity's components, its add callback with the spawn data (kind 1), then its setup callback with a scratch buffer (kind 2). Every machine runs it for every spawn, remote ones included; the entity is not in the network id map yet
SpawnEntityAddComponents.source: HellForge research (build 25480438): SpawnEntity's call at 0xFDC25A, the callback table filled at 0x551B60

SpawnEntityFinishComponents.meaning: SpawnEntity's last component pass: each of the new entity's components' finish callback (kind 3), after every component exists and the entity is in the network id map. A detour that runs after the original sees the entity fully set up, before SpawnEntity returns
SpawnEntityFinishComponents.source: HellForge research (build 25480438): SpawnEntity's call at 0xFDC2B1, the callback table filled at 0x551B60

params.name: ctx
params.meaning: the caller's second argument (through the thunk), passed on unchanged to each component's activate callbacks

ActivateEntity.meaning: Switches an entity on in this machine's world: finds it by network id, sets bit 0 of its record's flags (+0x14) and runs each of its components' activate callbacks (kinds 6, then 7), unless a tag or a session flag holds it back. The session calls it through LocalUser's entity callbacks (+0xB3D0, set at 0x134D470, via a thunk at 0xBA0670)
ActivateEntity.source: HellForge research (build 25480438): 0xFDBB40, its thunks at 0xBA0670 and 0xFDA130, the callback table filled at 0x551B60

params.name: ctx
params.meaning: the caller's second argument (through the thunk), passed on unchanged to each component's deactivate callbacks

DeactivateEntity.meaning: Switches an entity off in this machine's world: finds it by network id and, if it is on (bit 0 of its record's flags, +0x14), runs each of its components' deactivate callbacks (kinds 9, then 8) and clears the bit. The entity stays in the world. The session calls it through LocalUser's entity callbacks (+0xB3D8, set at 0x134D470, via a thunk at 0xBA0680)
DeactivateEntity.source: HellForge research (build 25480438): 0xFDBEA0, its thunks at 0xBA0680 and 0xFDA140, 0x581E10
